Subject: Log retention scope + evidence request for SOC2/SIG

Hi Priya / Ben —

Quick one from our security team as we prepare for VertexScale's annual SOC 2 re-assessment. We need confirmation on the retention and deletion controls that apply to tenant-scoped debug / inference logs for our hosted deployment: specifically where these logs are stored, retention windows, and the deletion proof process.

Key asks:
- Can you confirm the default retention for request/response logs vs ephemeral debug traces?
- Do you support tenant-level carveouts (we want a 90-day deletion SLA for debug traces only)?
- Please provide artifacts we can upload to our auditor: retention policy excerpt, runbook for 'proof of delete', and a sample manifest exported from your forensics pipeline showing a deletion event.

We have a tight deadline: final auditor package due by 2027-03-25. Can you let us know what you can turn around and an ETA?

Thanks,
Aisha Ramirez
Head of Security Programs
VertexScale

Hi Aisha / team —

Thanks — want to align expectations from the compliance side. A few notes and proposed deliverables:

Notes:
- SOC 2 auditors generally expect three classes of artifacts for retention/deletion: policy excerpts, operational evidence (manifests/logs showing deletion), and a runnable playbook/runbook. For SIG/CAIQ we map the same artifacts back to their questions.
- Tenant-level carveouts are supported for hosted customers as a configuration on our retention router, but they require a signed MSA amendment for retention variance if it changes default retention beyond our standard SLAs.
- KV cache is considered ephemeral system state and is not ordinarily included in long-term retention — we will clarify how / if any diagnostic snapshots are captured and where they land.

Deliverables we'll produce: 
1) retention_matrix.csv — row per artifact type, column for default TTL, tenant-carveout allowed (Y/N), location (S3 bucket/prefix), and sample evidence file name.
2) proof_of_delete_runbook.pdf — step-by-step (engineering + infra) including how manifests are generated, signing, and CAIQ/SIG mapping notes.
3) forensics_sample_manifest.txt — an anonymized example of a deletion event (object keys redacted) the auditor can validate.

Action items: Ben, can you pull a redacted sample manifest and a short set of S3 deletion logs (single tenant sample) and drop them to the Drive link Priya will share? We should avoid including PII in the artifacts.

I can also draft the MSA amendment language for a 90-day tenant carveout if VertexScale needs it.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Compliance Analyst
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: security-mapping-notes.docx (internal planning)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Log retention scope + evidence request for SOC2/SIG

Aisha — attaching the items Marissa and Priya outlined. Deliverables included below and uploaded to the Drive link.

Deliverables (attached / Drive):
- retention_matrix.csv (attached) — maps log classes and default TTLs; marks tenant-carveout column.
- forensics_sample_manifest.txt (attached) — redacted manifest showing delete_event_id, timestamp, signed_hash.
- proof_of_delete_runbook.pdf (Drive) — operational runbook + signer checklist.
- forensics_export_samples.zip (Drive, stub) — redacted samples used for auditor inspection.

Notes/assumptions:
- The 'debug traces' you referenced are stored in the ephemeral-debug bucket (one tenant-scoped prefix per customer). Default TTL for ephemeral-debug is 30 days; we can support a 90-day tenant carveout via MSA amendment and a signed change order.
- KV cache snapshots are not persisted long-term in production; occasional diagnostic snapshots are stored in a restricted bucket with 7-day retention.
- We generated a redacted sample manifest for a deletion performed on 2027-02-20 to demonstrate the proof-of-delete flow — see manifest id DEL-20270220-XYZ in the attached manifest.

Next steps:
- Aisha, confirm whether VertexScale needs us to proceed with drafting the MSA amendment for a 90-day tenant carveout.
- If yes, Priya will coordinate commercial / legal and Marissa will sign off on compliance language.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m call if your auditor needs a walkthrough.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Forensics & Instrumentation
Redwood Inference
